huntington-applied.tagline: Software, simulation systems and secure infrastructure for teams doing advanced research and engineering.
about: Huntington Applied builds software and systems for advanced research: platforms, tools and infrastructure for organizations doing complex scientific and engineering work. Its stated aim is to shorten the path from research to systems people can use.

Its work spans simulation and modeling, security infrastructure for research environments, development tooling and research operations. The featured platform is Boltzmann, a collaborative multiphysics simulation platform that pairs forward simulation with inverse device design.

Engagements are limited to software and simulation development: custom research infrastructure, simulation platforms, platform licensing and research partnerships. The work is carried out by the members who build and maintain the company's own platforms.
Membership is lifetime and invite-only, with new members approved unanimously by existing members. A Models page catalogs open neural-net surrogate weights published across its research projects.
huntington-applied.studio: Butts Studios designed the identity and the website.

runwae-apparel.tagline: A streetwear label that treats each piece as a work of art, under the line "Everybody Influences".
about: Runwae Apparel is a streetwear brand built around the line "Everybody Influences". Its first magazine, Issue No. 1, published October 2020, placed the garments inside gilt-framed Renaissance and Baroque paintings.
That idea carries through the brand: a dripping-R seal in coral on charcoal, the full Runwae Apparel name set in a serif face, and gilt used for frames and rules.

The apparel comes in two lines. Fall '21 is the original line, with tees and hoodies such as Crafting, True Grit, Poison and Pave. The Little Things is a hand-drawn line built on the idea that in life, it's all about the little things.
runwae-apparel.studio: Butts Studios designed the identity, the print pieces and the product imagery.

dailyaitoll.tagline: A daily, sourced record of job cuts that public reporting links to AI adoption.
about: Daily AI Toll keeps a running record of publicly reported job displacement linked to artificial intelligence. It aggregates the events, verifies them where possible and presents the count plainly, updated daily.

Collection is automated: an AI system scans public news sources each night, and every entry carries a source link, an excerpt, a causality class (direct, contributing or inferred) and a confidence score.

The methodology describes the figures as a lower-bound estimate, since many AI-related job losses go unreported or are attributed to other causes. The site asks readers to verify the data before relying on it.
Trends charts the cumulative and monthly totals, and the full event dataset is available as a licensed CSV for research or commercial use.
dailyaitoll.studio: Butts Studios designed the identity and the data site.

latarence.tagline: The one-page personal site of Latarence Butts, PhD.
about: Latarence is the personal site of Latarence Butts, PhD. It is a single page that carries his name, a hand-drawn mark and a link to his LinkedIn profile.
In light mode the page shows a pen portrait on paper; in dark mode it swaps in the L² mark drawn in chalk on ink. The name is set in handwriting above a small monospace footer.

ridgefield.tagline: An engineering firm for hardware, software, simulation and AI systems built to perform under real-world conditions.
about: Ridgefield is an engineering firm for systems that have to perform under real-world conditions. It works across five areas: hardware, software, simulation, AI and operations.

The hardware practice covers RF front-ends, antenna arrays, LTCC multilayer packaging and radar. Software spans embedded firmware, signal processing and full-stack platforms, and the simulation work covers device, site and propagation modeling.

Engagements start with a system assessment that looks for where systems or operations underperform, followed by design, build and ongoing technical advisory. Ridgefield describes itself as working at the seam between defense and commercial engineering, based in West Palm Beach, Florida.
Its Demos page runs two of its systems in the browser: Vantage Echo, a reflective metasurface you can steer, and Covey, a replay of a distributed radar swarm imaging a city block in simulation.

signals-institute.tagline: Building long-term pathways into advanced technology, engineering and scientific fields, based in West Palm Beach.
about: The Signals Institute is building long-term pathways into advanced technology, engineering and scientific fields. Based in West Palm Beach, it works through youth engagement, veteran transition and community programs.

Its approach rests on three pillars: engagement, exposure and transition. The Institute plans to build consistent relationships within schools, community organizations and faith-based networks, introduce participants to new fields and mentors, and support real transitions into advanced training and careers.

The name comes from its founding idea: signals are indicators of change, need and opportunity. The Institute is looking to partner with libraries, schools, community centers and city facilities that can host its programs.
signals-institute.studio: Butts Studios designed the identity and the website.

landslide.tagline: Stochastic simulation that couples weather, financial, population, sentiment and physical domains to model how shocks cascade.
about: Landslide is a stochastic simulation platform that links five domains (weather, financial, population, sentiment and physical) through Monte Carlo coupling, so a disruption in one can be traced into the others.

It was built around what the site calls the prediction paradox, where forecasts change behavior and so change the outcomes being forecast. Extreme value theory is used to model rare, high-impact tail events.

Automated findings stream alongside each run and mark prediction stalls and distribution hotspots on the map. The live demo uses an approximate AI surrogate on sample scenarios, which the page labels as an estimate rather than a full simulation.
Landslide publishes trained surrogate models with model cards, an open benchmark with a public leaderboard, and a desktop app for macOS and Linux.

runwae.tagline: A platform for agreements between brands and influencers, from proposal to verified post to payment.
about: Runwae is a platform for agreements between brands and influencers. Brands post marketing opportunities with a set budget, and influencers find opportunities from brands in their industry and send proposals.
Each gig follows one agreement process: the influencer submits a proposal, the brand accepts it, the influencer posts the agreed content, the brand verifies the post, and the influencer is paid.

Agreements, brand-to-creator messaging and payments sit in one place, with a profile that holds all of a creator's gigs. The Runwae blog carries guides on pricing and finding influencers alongside interviews with creators.

boltzmann.tagline: Collaborative multiphysics simulation with ML-accelerated solving, inverse device design and real-time 3D visualization.
about: Boltzmann is a collaborative multiphysics simulation platform covering electromagnetic, thermal, mechanical and semiconductor physics in one place. Simulations run in the cloud from the browser, with real-time 3D visualization.

Alongside forward simulation, Boltzmann offers inverse device design: describe target specifications and it generates a device architecture with regions, contacts, materials and boundary conditions, ready to simulate.

The Simulation Studio shows convergence, fields and solver status while a run is in progress, and a browser-based IDE edits device configurations with side-by-side 3D viewers. Teams can publish interactive results and track how they are used.

Trained neural surrogates give fast estimates of device fields. The live demo generates a silicon PN diode and runs those surrogates over it, labeled on the page as an approximation of a full physics solve.

chrona.tagline: Realtime RF and SAR scenario simulation in 3D, with AI-driven RF intelligence and inverse scenario design.
about: Chrona builds dynamic RF and SAR scenarios that run in realtime and in full 3D. Users compose terrain, platforms and emitters, then watch propagation, returns and geometry change as the scenario plays out.

Scenarios can be wargamed with AI in the loop or run in reverse: start from the outcome you want and let Chrona optimize the scenarios that reach it. Propagation is terrain-based, using ITU-R P.2001 with multipath and atmospheric effects.

Chrona also pairs emulated scenarios with real RF receivers for hardware-in-the-loop testing of localization algorithms in repeatable conditions. Its live demo predicts a received-power coverage field from a trained model, offered as a preview before a full electromagnetic solve.

blacklab.tagline: Predicts the physical state of a place by fusing a physics engine, live sensors and fast learned surrogates.
about: Blacklab predicts a physical field over a place, such as the strength of a signal, the presence of an object or how either changes over the next few minutes. It fuses a deterministic physics engine, live sensors and fast learned surrogates into one estimate with per-point confidence.
Radio, camera, LiDAR, radar, audio and weather feeds pass through a common adapter format called PixelCloud. RF is described as the first validated physics domain.
A tiling and attribution design lets many nodes predict a shared area together, with results checked through consensus. People can run the desktop client to contribute compute to the network.
The live demo estimates where a tracked object goes next, or how a transmitter covers an area, and is labeled a fast approximate estimate on a fixed scene.

raphael.tagline: Research intelligence that forecasts research trajectories and designs the teams and resources behind breakthroughs.
about: Raphael is a research intelligence platform. It uses forward simulation to forecast how research fields and their impact may develop, and inverse design to propose the teams, resources and collaboration structures that could lead to a breakthrough.
It continuously ingests new literature from ArXiv, Semantic Scholar and PubMed, and renders citation and concept networks as interactive 3D knowledge graphs that update as new research arrives.

Graph, map and experiment studios launch runs and show results live, with pluggable deterministic and stochastic engines. The live demo classifies a research paper into one of seven fields and is labeled an approximate classifier.

sage.tagline: Multi-scale biological simulation from molecules to tissues, with ML-accelerated molecular dynamics and target-driven design.
about: Sage is a cloud platform for biological simulation across four scales: molecular, protein, cellular and tissue. Researchers load a structure from RCSB or draft one from a natural-language prompt, choose a force field and conditions, and watch trajectories unfold in a live 3D viewer.

Physics-informed neural networks learn from molecular dynamics runs to speed up simulation while keeping biochemical constraints. Sage describes itself as the step after structure prediction: it takes a known structure and simulates how it moves, binds and reacts.

The Optimization Studio runs target-driven campaigns that tune a structure toward properties such as binding affinity and stability. The site presents fully de novo design from target specifications as the broader vision.

Teams can scrub and replay trajectories, review per-residue analytics, share interactive results and automate work through a REST API with Python and JavaScript clients. The public demo uses an approximate AI surrogate on sample complexes to estimate binding affinity.

farad.tagline: Defensive cyber simulation for training and benchmarking autonomous defender agents, building toward privacy-preserving collaborative defense.
about: Farad is a defensive cybersecurity platform built around simulation. Today it trains and evaluates cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning defenders against adversaries scripted over a modeled network.

Five specialized agents cover detection, response, hardening, forensics and threat hunting. Benchmark reports reference MITRE-aligned threats and public references such as CAGE-4, and a replayable spatial view shows what a defender did and why.

The longer-term aim is collaborative defense through federated learning and zero-knowledge proofs, so organizations can share threat intelligence while keeping their infrastructure private. The site states that the proof circuits are implemented and that the cross-organization exchange is on the roadmap.
The public demo uses a trained detector to read the stage and severity of synthetic attack scenarios as a fast estimate.

tiffany.tagline: Central monitoring for research infrastructure: streaming metrics ingestion, time-series analytics and live dashboards in one platform.
about: Tiffany is a central monitoring platform for research infrastructure. It ingests metrics over a binary TCP protobuf stream, as well as length-prefixed JSON and StatsD over UDP, and shows them in live dashboards with drill-down views.

Storage is split by workload: PostgreSQL for transactional data, TimescaleDB for time series with continuous aggregation, and Redis for caching and sessions. Tiffany reports its own health through the same pipeline it uses for every other service.

A REST API with OpenAPI documentation, a CLI for operations tasks, an operator console for entitlements and LLM cost tracking, and an autonomous missions engine for routine development work complete the platform. It is offered under a one-time enterprise license with self-hosted, on-premise and hybrid deployment.

nods.tagline: Terminal workspace orchestration: define panes, directories and commands once in YAML, then launch the whole layout with one command.
about: NODS is a terminal workspace orchestrator. Developers describe windows, panes, working directories and startup commands once in YAML, then launch the full environment with a single command.

It drives tmux, gnome-terminal, Terminator and Konsole, locally or on remote servers over SSH with persistent tmux sessions. The same definition can start an AI assistant in each pane and inject its prompt, coordinating agentic work across machines through a shared ledger.
Workspace configurations can be version-controlled and shared across a team, and session metrics track launch times and usage. The CLI is open source and runs on macOS and Linux.

chief.tagline: No-code programming of JavaCard and PIV smart cards, for hardware-bound credentials an organization can issue and manage itself.
about: Chief is a platform for programming JavaCard and PIV smart cards through a guided, no-code wizard. It handles the cryptographic steps so teams can issue hardware-bound credentials using their own readers and cards.

Chief sets up a certificate authority for the organization, generates each keypair on the card and signs its certificate, so the private key stays on the hardware. Administrators can revoke lost cards, renew expiring certificates and distribute CRL and OCSP updates.

Card Studio lets people design a card in 3D before programming it, and a library of pre-built applets covers web login, document signing, VPN, identity badges and physical access. The site describes Chief as an early-stage product.

OCR extracts text with broad language support, and full-text search covers file names and document contents with highlighted snippets, folders and filters. Teams share folders and documents with role-based access.

Developers can build with a REST API, a CLI for terminals and CI, and a JavaScript package that runs the scanning pipeline on-device in the browser. The site describes Document Scanner as an early-stage product.

Built-in AI tools check facts, score source credibility and flag logical fallacies. Typing a topic generates a starter map with a central claim, premises, evidence, a counter-argument and a conclusion, which the group then examines and extends.
Rigor is aimed at policy and advocacy teams, researchers, public institutions and educators, and finished maps can be published for anyone to explore.

Creators submit content for approval inside the platform, with feedback tools and version tracking. Payments are held in escrow and released by milestone once deliverables are approved and published.

Participation is verified through GPS presence, timestamped media, witness attestation and transaction receipts, and each action is recorded with a signed participation certificate. Threaded deliberation and signed records build an audit trail that stakeholders can review.

Coalitions can run multi-organization campaigns with shared dashboards, and the Campaign Studio scopes a campaign to a region drawn on a map. Civic organizations can also run member elections with verifiable voting.

Content generation uses defined personas with consistent voices for tutorials, release notes and community updates, and drafts pass through a human review workflow. Sentiment analysis follows community mood across platforms and surfaces emerging concerns.

tillio.tagline: A living cap table for projects that grow on contribution: agree the split, log the work, watch equity update.
about: Tillio is a living cap table for projects that grow on contribution. Founders, contributors and advisors sign one equity agreement that sets vesting, milestones and category weights.

Team members log contributions as they happen, from code and design to investor intros and checks. An AI evaluation engine drafts a value and a rationale for each entry, and the project owner approves, edits or overrides it.

Approved entries update the split that everyone on the team sees, payouts follow the ledger over Stripe and bank rails, and every entry has a comment thread and a dispute window. Tillio is in alpha, with a CLI and a GitHub Actions workflow for logging work from code.

sentinel.tagline: Integrity scanning for code, docs and configuration: detect corruption, trace where it started, and repair it safely.
about: Sentinel scans codebases for integrity issues: corruption, typo-class defects, copy drift, broken references and configuration inconsistencies across code, documentation and config files.

It runs quick, deep, ecosystem and CI/CD scan modes against a built-in pattern library, classifies each finding by severity, and opens guided repair sessions to apply fixes. Git history forensics help trace when an issue entered the codebase and how far it spread.
The same engine powers a CLI for CI and pre-commit hooks, a desktop app and a web dashboard, so findings stay consistent across all three.
